childhood: I grew up with salt in my hair and sand in my shoes. Every day of my childhood smelled of the sea.
We'd race the tide as children. Whoever got wet first did the washing up.
I learned to swim before I could walk properly. That's how it is on the coast.
family: My family still lives by the harbour in {home_town}. They think inland people are a bit strange.
My {kin} sends me shells in every letter. I've a jar of them by my bed.
background: I left the coast because the fishing was failing. I miss the sea every single day.
Inland was meant to be a short adventure. That was a while ago now.
nature: The river's lovely, but I miss waves. Rivers only go one way.
Gulls used to wake me every morning. Now it's roosters. I'm adjusting.
hopes: One day I'll take someone from here to see the sea. Their face, the first time. That's what I want to see.

stories: There was a storm on the coast when I was young. The worst in fifty years.
Every boat in {home_town} was out. My {kin} included.
The whole village stood on the cliff with lanterns all night, so they could find their way home.
[happy]Every single boat came back. We still light lanterns on that night, every year.

childhood: I grew up so high up the clouds came through the village. We'd walk through them to school.
Mountain children learn two things first: where to step, and when to turn back.
We had goats instead of dogs. They climbed better and complained louder.
family: My family still keeps goats up in {home_town}. They think the valley's too soft for anyone.
My {kin} could climb anything. I used to follow and get stuck. Often.
background: Mountain winters are long and hard. One year I decided I'd rather be warm.
I came down the passes with a pack and a pair of boots. The boots didn't survive. I did.
nature: Down here the air's so thick I can taste it. Up there it's thin and sharp like ice.
I miss the silence of the peaks. The valley's beautiful, but it's never quiet.
hopes: I want to climb the hill behind the village one dawn and see the mountains from here. Just to wave.

stories: When I was young, I got lost in a snowstorm on the pass above {home_town}.
I couldn't see my own hands. I just sat down in the snow and waited.
A goat found me. Our old nanny goat, Bramble. She'd come looking.
[happy]I held on to her horns and she walked me home. I've never eaten goat cheese without saying thank you since.

childhood: I grew up on a river so wide you couldn't see the other side in the mist.
We had boats instead of carts. I knew how to row before I knew my letters.
Every summer the river market came to {home_town}. A hundred boats tied together. A floating town.
family: My family are boat people. My {kin} still runs the ferry in {home_town}.
We were loud, my family. Big, loud and always on the water.
background: The river flooded and took our house. I decided to try somewhere higher.
I followed this river upstream. It was a whim. I'm glad I did.
nature: The river here's young and fast. Back home it's old, wide and slow.
I still dream about water lilies. They covered the river like a blanket in summer.
hopes: I'd love to row back down to {home_town} one day, all the way, and show my {kin} how far I've come.

stories: Every spring in {home_town}, we had the lantern race.
Every child made a paper boat with a candle in it, and we set them on the river at dusk.
The one that went furthest without sinking won a whole honeycake.
[laughing]I never won. Not once. My boats sank in about a minute. But I still make one every spring.

childhood: I grew up where the land is flat as a table. You could see a storm coming for days.
We rode horses everywhere. A plains child gets their first horse before their first shoes.
The grass was taller than me as a child. We'd play hide and seek for hours.
family: My family keep horses out on the plains near {home_town}. Dozens of them.
My {kin} taught me to read the sky. Out there, the sky is everything.
background: The plains are lovely but lonely. I wanted to live somewhere with neighbours nearby.
A long drought came. The herds suffered. I came west to find better land.
nature: Hills! I'm still not used to hills. My legs ache all the time.
I miss the huge skies. Here the hills hold the sky in. It feels cosy, but small.
hopes: I want a horse again. Just one. To ride out at dawn, like I used to.

stories: On the plains, there's a night every summer called the Long Watch.
Everyone in {home_town} lies in the grass and watches the stars fall.
My {kin} said each falling star is someone, somewhere, making a wish.
[happy]The first summer here, I lay on the hill and watched. I made a wish about this place. It's coming true.

childhood: Up north, winter nights last forever. We told stories to keep the dark away.
I grew up mending nets with frozen fingers. Here the summers feel like a gift.
We had a saying in {home_town}: 'the sea gives, the sea takes, the sea doesn't apologise'.
family: My family are fisherfolk, back to my great-great-grandparents. My {kin} still sails.
Northern families are quiet. We say a lot without saying anything.
background: The fish went further out every year. In the end, I followed the rivers south instead.
I wanted to see a summer that lasted more than a month.
nature: The trees here are so green. Up north, everything's grey and blue.
I saw the northern lights every winter as a child. I miss them more than anything.
hopes: I want to see the lights again someday. Maybe I'll bring someone. Maybe you.

stories: One winter in {home_town}, the sea froze right out to the islands.
We walked across the ice to the island where my {kin} lived. Three hours on the ice.
Halfway, the lights came out. Green and purple, all across the sky.
[happy]We just stood there on the frozen sea, all of us, saying nothing. I'll never forget it.

childhood: I grew up in the city. Streets everywhere, people everywhere, noise everywhere.
City children play in alleys and rooftops. I'd never seen a cow until I was twelve.
I could find my way through a thousand streets in {home_town}, but I'd never seen a wild deer.
family: My family run a shop in the city. My {kin} thinks I've gone mad, living in a village.
City families are scattered. Here everyone eats together. I'm still getting used to it.
background: The city got too loud. Too crowded. I needed to hear myself think.
I came looking for somewhere I could see the stars. You can't see them in the city.
nature: The first night here, the silence kept me awake. Now I can't sleep without it.
I'd never picked an apple from a tree before I came here. I cried. Don't laugh.
hopes: I hope I never go back to the city. I hope I visit, though. To brag.

stories: In the city, you don't know your neighbours. I lived in one room for years.
Then one winter I got sick, and nobody came. Not for days.
When I got better, I packed a bag and walked until the streets ended.
[happy]Here, I got a cold last month, and four people brought me soup on the first day. Four.

childhood: I grew up on a farm, just like this valley but three valleys over. Same hills, different cows.
Farm children work from the moment they can carry a bucket. I didn't mind. Much.
We had a big old barn at {home_town}. I'd hide in the hay and read when I should've been working.
family: My family still farm the old land. My {kin} took over when our parents got too old.
There were too many of us for one farm. Someone had to go. I volunteered.
background: The farm went to my {kin}, so I walked over the hills looking for land of my own.
Three valleys isn't far. But it's far enough to start fresh.
nature: The soil here's different. Darker, richer. My family would be jealous.
Same birds as home, mostly. It's comforting. Like old friends followed me.
hopes: I want my family to visit and see what I've made here. Just once.

stories: Back at {home_town}, we had an old ox called Patience.
She was slow, grumpy and the strongest animal I've ever seen.
One spring the cart got stuck in the river with my {kin} on it, and Patience pulled the whole thing out alone.
[happy]We gave her a crown of flowers. She ate it. Fair enough.

childhood: I grew up on the road. Every few weeks, a new place. A wagon was my house.
Caravan children learn to make friends fast. You never know how long you'll stay.
I learned to juggle, cook and mend wheels before I was ten.
family: My family travel with the caravan still. My {kin} sends letters from every town they pass.
Caravan people are your family, whether you're related or not.
background: The caravan stopped near here for repairs. I fell asleep under a tree. When I woke up, they'd gone.
They didn't forget me, exactly. They just counted wrong. I decided to stay instead of chasing them.
nature: I've seen a hundred valleys. This is the first one I didn't want to leave.
I used to sleep under the stars every night. A roof still feels strange sometimes.
hopes: One day the caravan will come back this way. I want them to see I've found a home.

stories: The caravan had a tradition: every new town, someone tells a story at the fire.
One night it was my turn. I was eight. I was terrified.
I made up a tale about a dragon who just wanted a friend. My {kin} cried.
[happy]I've told it in fifty towns since. I'll tell it here, if you'd like.

childhood: I grew up in the deep forest, where the trees are so tall the sun only reaches the ground at noon.
Forest children learn every bird call. I can still whistle a dozen.
Our houses in {home_town} were built into the trees. I learned to climb before I learned to walk.
family: My family are forest people. My {kin} knows every path through the woods.
We were taught to take only what the forest offers freely.
background: The forest settlements are very quiet. I wanted to see more people, more sky.
Loggers came to our forest. The settlement scattered. I came here.
nature: Open fields still make me nervous. Too much sky. I keep close to the trees.
I can tell what time it is by which birds are singing.
hopes: I hope the forests here stay wild. I'll fight for that, if I have to.

stories: In the forest near {home_town}, there's a tree we called the Grandmother.
She was so wide it took twelve people holding hands to circle her.
Every child in the settlement was given a name under her branches.
[happy]I go to the oldest tree in every forest I find and tell it my name. It feels like being welcomed.

childhood: I grew up in the marshes, where the land and water can't decide which is which.
We walked on stilts through the shallows to get anywhere. I was very good at it.
We harvested salt in {home_town}. My fingers were always cracked and white.
family: My family still harvest salt. My {kin} can taste the difference between a good batch and a bad one.
Marsh families are close. We had to be. The land was hard.
background: The sea came in further every year and took the salt pans. We had to leave.
I wanted ground that stays put under my feet.
nature: Here the ground is solid. I keep stamping on it to check.
I miss the marsh birds. Thousands of them, rising all at once at dawn.
hopes: I want to bring my family here one day. On solid ground. Where it's safe.

stories: Once a year in {home_town}, all the birds of the marsh would gather.
Millions of them. They'd fly up together at dawn and turn the sky black.
My {kin} and I would lie on our backs and listen to the sound of their wings. Like rain going up.
[happy]I've never heard anything like it since. I hope I do again someday.

childhood: I was born right here. This valley's all I've ever known. I think it's the best place in the world.
I've been playing by the river since before I could talk. I know every stone.
The founders watched me grow up. They're like extra parents. Extra strict ones.
family: My parents met here. I'm a real village child. First generation!
Everyone here's family, in a way. I've got about twenty aunts and uncles who aren't.
background: I've never left the valley. One day I want to see what's beyond the hills. Then come back.
Being born here means everyone knows everything I've ever done. Everything.
nature: I know every tree in this valley. I've climbed most of them.
The best fishing spot is by the big rock. Don't tell anyone. Secret.
hopes: I hope this place keeps growing. I want my children to play by the same river.

stories: When I was really small, I got lost in the woods past the field.
I wasn't scared at first. Then it got dark and I was very scared.
The whole village came looking. With lanterns. Calling my name.
[happy]When they found me, nobody shouted. They just carried me home. That's when I knew this place was home.

childhood: I grew up far away, but my family always talked about one day being together again.
As a child, I imagined what it'd be like to live near my family. It's better than I imagined.
I grew up hearing stories about my family, the ones who'd moved away. I always wondered what they were like.
family: My family invited me here. I'd never have found this place without them.
It's strange, being near family again after so long. Wonderful. Strange.
Family's a funny thing. You can be apart for years and still argue about the same old things within a day.
background: A letter came asking me to come and live here. I packed that same day.
I came because family asked. I'm staying because I love it.
Before the letter came, I lived alone in a small rented room. It was quiet. Too quiet.
nature: Everyone told me about this valley in their letters. It's even prettier than they said.
hopes: I hope I can make this place home for myself, not just because family's here.
One day, I'd like to be the one who writes the letter. Inviting someone else home.
seasons: My first season here, family showed me everything: the river, the woods, the best spot to watch the sunset.
evenings: Eating supper with family again. I forgot how loud it is. I love how loud it is.
worries: [worried]I worry I'm only here because I'm family. I want people to like me for me.

stories: When the letter came asking me to come here, I almost said no.
I'd been on my own so long. I thought I'd forgotten how to live near family.
Then I read the last line. 'There's a chair at our table with your name carved on it.'
[happy]There really was. There still is. I sit in it every night.
